questions.question: ________ was appointed Chief Justice of India with effect from 18 November 2019.
questions.solution:
__**Sharad Arvind Bobde**__ was appointed **Chief Justice of India** with effect from **18 November 2019.**

__
 
• He is serving as the 47th Chief Justice of India.
 
• He is a** former Chief Justice of the High Court of Madhya Pradesh. **
 
• He was **a member of the five-court Constitutional Court**, which heard and issued a judgment dated 9 November 2019 on the land dispute case of Ram Janmabhoomi-Babri Masjid.
 
• **Ranjan Gogoi **was the 46th Chief Justice of India.
 
• **Ashok Bhushan** was the 31st Chief Justice of the Kerala High Court.
 
• **Dipak Misra **was the 45th Chief Justice of India.

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT a type of sacrifice performed by kings in ancient India to establish their position?
questions.solution:
__**Muvendavelan**__ was **NOT **a type of sacrifice performed by **kings in ancient India to establish their position.**

 
• **Muvendavelan** was a famous military officer of the Chola Empire, known for his generous donation to the numerous temples where he had been deployed by the king.
 
• **The Rajasuya** is connected with the consecration of the King and is prescribed as a way of maintaining the king's sovereignty.
 
• It involves a game of throwing dice, in which the king is enthroned and the world is regenerated.
 
• **Vajapeya Yagna** has been performed to preserve peace in the state. It's the highest form of Soma Yajna.
 
• **Ashvamedha Yagna** was performed by the King for fertility and strength in the kingdom.
 
• It is a rite of horse sacrifice accompanied by the** practice of the Vedic religion of the Shrauta.** This has been used by ancient Indian kings to assert their colonial supremacy.

questions.question: Article _____ of the Constitution of India deals with provisions related to the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes.
questions.solution:
__**Article 244(1)**__ of the Constitution of **India deals with provisions related to the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes.**

 
• The provisions of the Fifth Schedule shall extend to
 the **administration and control of the Scheduled Areas and of the Scheduled Tribes **in every State other than **Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram.**
 
• **Article 244(2)** provisions of the Sixth Schedule shall extend to the administration and control of tribal areas of Meghalaya, Tripura, Assam, and Mizoram.
 
• **According to Article 222(1),** The President can, after consulting the Chief Justice of India, move a Judge from one High Court to any other High Court.
 
• **According to Article 222(2)**, When a judge has been or has been moved, he or she shall, for the time of which he or she serves, since the beginning of the Constitution Act (Fifteenth Amendment) of 1963.

questions.question: The spice, cinnamon, is native to ________.
questions.solution:
**The spice, cinnamon**, is native to **__Sri Lanka.__**

 
• **Cinnamon** is a spice produced from the inner bark of many varieties of **trees in the genus Cinnamomum.**
 
• It is used primarily as an aromatic condiment and flavouring ingredient in a **wide variety of desserts, sweet and savoury desserts, breakfast cereals, snack foods, tea, and traditional foods.**
 
• **Indonesia and China produced 75% of the world's cinnamon supply in 2016.**
 
• Four countries accounted for 99% of the world as a whole in 2017: **Indonesia, China, Vietnam and Sri Lanka.**

questions.question: ______ was executed at Lahore in November 1915 for his role in the Ghadar Conspiracy in February 1915.
questions.solution:

questions.question: Crocodiles have a ______ chambered heart.
questions.solution:
**Crocodiles** have a **__four-chambered__ heart.**

 
• Adaptation to their maximum portion of the life cycle is done in water since they need to minimize the oxygen loss when submerged and the **four-chambered hearts decrease the heartbeat by 2-3/minute** and normalize this rate when the crocodile is above water.
 
• The crocodile may have the **most complex circulatory vertebrate system. **
 
• This has a four-chambered heart and two ventricles, an uncommon characteristic between the current reptiles, and both the left and the right aorta, which are connected by a hole called the **Panizza Foramen.**
 
• Crocodiles belong to **Crocodylidae family.**

• After Theodore Roosevelt, he was the second non-European to win a Nobel Prize.
 
• **King George V **was awarded the Knighthood in 1915 of Birthday Honours, but Tagore renounced it after the 1919 massacre of Jallianwala Bagh.
 
• **Jana Gana Mana** is an Indian national anthem.
 
• It was originally **written by the poet Rabindranath Tagore as Bharoto Bhagyo Bidhata in Bengali.**

questions.question: The Government of India launched the ________ Initiative on 16 January 2016, with the objective of supporting entrepreneurs, building a robust start-up ecosystem and transforming India into a country of job creators instead of job seekers.
questions.solution:
**The Government of India** launched the **__Start-up India__** Initiative **on 16 January 2016, with the objective of supporting entrepreneurs,** building a robust start-up ecosystem, and transforming India into a country of job creators instead of job seekers.

 
• The Government of India launched the** "Start-up India" campaign in New Delhi on 16 January 2016. **
 
• The aim of this event was at celebrating the entrepreneurial spirit of the youth of the **country and attended by CEOs and founders of the biggest start-ups (over 1500) from across the world.**
 
• The Department of Industrial Policy and Promotion (DIPP) coordinated this event along with Invest India and Start-up ecosystem players iSpirt, YourStory, NASSCOM, SheThePeople.tv and the Kairos Society and the FICCI and CII Youth wings.
 
• 
 
The closing session addressed by the** Honorable Prime Minister of India, Shri Narendra Modi, **who officially launched the project and unveil the Start-up Action Plan.

• This is the** third-largest Buddhist pilgrimage site** in Burma after **the Mahamuni Pagoda and Shwedagon Pagoda.**

questions.question: Which of the following is an inert gas most commonly found in light bulbs?
questions.solution:
__**Argon**__ is an inert gas most commonly found in **light bulbs.**

 
• **Argon improves bulb life by avoiding too rapid** a degradation of the tungsten filaments.
 
• **Nitrogen** also added in incandescent light bulbs at** the rate of 7%.**
 
• Argon has a comparable **low breakdown voltage**, applying a small amount of nitrogen to avoid arcing between the supports of the filaments.
 
• Other gasses like hydrogen, neon, nitrogen and krypton are also used for **illumination purposes.**
 
• **High-brightness "halogen" **bulbs use argon mixture and a limited quantity of halogen, usually bromine or iodine.
